# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 77 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 77 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_077_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 7

**1** After a few days I saw him in the same plain where I had also seen the shepherds; and he said to me, "What do you seek?" **2** I said to him, "Lord, I ask that you command the shepherd who punishes to depart from my house, for he greatly afflicts me." **3** "It is necessary for you to be afflicted," he replied, "for thus the glorious angel commanded regarding you, wishing that you be tested." **4** "But why, Lord? What evil have I done that I should be handed over to this angel?" **5** "Listen," he said; "your sins are many, yet not so many that you should be delivered to this angel. But your household has committed great iniquities and sins, and the glorious angel has been embittered over their deeds, and so commanded that you be afflicted for a time, in order that they too might repent and be cleansed from every worldly desire. **6** When they repent and are cleansed, the angel of punishment will depart." **7** I said to him, "Lord, if they have acted in such a way that the glorious angel has been embittered, what have I done?" He answered, "There is no other way for them to be afflicted unless you, as head of the household, are afflicted; for when you are afflicted they are necessarily afflicted as well, but when you are comfortable they have no share in affliction." **8** I said, "But Lord, behold — they have repented with their whole heart." **9** "I know," he said, "that they have repented with their whole heart. But do you suppose that the sins of those who repent are forgiven immediately? Not at all — the one who repents must discipline his own soul and be deeply humbled in all his conduct and pass through many kinds of affliction. And if he endures the afflictions that come upon him, he who created all things and invested them with power will certainly be moved with compassion and grant some remedy. **10** And this will come about when he sees the heart of every penitent clean from every evil. It is therefore beneficial for you and for your household to be afflicted now. But why do I say much? You must be afflicted as the angel of the Lord commanded when he delivered you to me. Give thanks to the Lord for this — that he judged you worthy to reveal the affliction beforehand, so that knowing it in advance you might endure it with strength."

---

### Translator's Note
Similitude 7 is the shortest of the ten similitudes, functioning as a theological bridge. The key doctrinal point is that suffering is not arbitrary punishment but redemptive discipline (*thlipsis*) coordinated at the angelic level. The "glorious angel" who presides over Hermas's household is distinct from the punishing shepherd; both serve the same divine economy of repentance. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's formal register while incorporating PNEUMA's clarity on the household-discipline dynamic.
